nudge.pointer-only.evidence: The waker never types: it starts mail nudge, and the fleet types its own one pointer line. Against the fake, two sessions holding different mail were each rung with the same one line, no control character and no line of either body. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13), which plays the contract in this waker's header. STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person, in a proof run (horde wake run -Proof -Target <session id> -Once): one idle session with unread mail is typed exactly the one pointer line, and no part of the mail's body.

state.box.evidence: mail state -To reads the session's pane for the box. Against the fake, an empty box read yes and a box holding text read no; for a session that is no candidate the pane is not read and the box is answered unknown, never yes. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13), which plays the contract in this waker's header. STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person, in a proof run (horde wake run -Proof -Target <session id> -Once): a session with text in its input box reads no and is not nudged, and one with an empty box reads yes.

state.turn.evidence: mail state -To reads the session's pane for the turn. Against the fake, a resting session read no and one in a turn read yes. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13), which plays the contract in this waker's header. STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person, in a proof run (horde wake run -Proof -Target <session id> -Once): a session in the middle of a turn reads yes and is not nudged, and a resting one reads no.

reach.unseen.evidence: mail nudge finds the pane and the terminal instance itself, from the fleet's own records, so it needs nothing this watcher saw since a restore. Against the fake, a session seated as not seen since a restore was rung once. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13), which plays the contract in this waker's header. STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person, in a proof run (horde wake run -Proof -Target <session id> -Once): a session that has not taken a turn since a restore is rung.

nudge.guarded.evidence: THE BOX IS GUARDED AT TYPING TIME, IDLE ONLY AT THE START OF THE COMMAND (read from the fleet's code, 2026-10-13): mail nudge re-reads the input box inside its send lock, just before the first key, and types nothing into a box that is not empty; it reads idle once, before it resolves the pane, so a session that goes busy between that reading and the keys gets the pointer line typed while it is mid-turn, where it queues behind the turn. It answers busy for a box that is not empty and for a session not idle at its start. Against the fake, a nudge sent straight at a session with text in its box, and at one mid-turn, typed nothing and answered busy, while a resting one was rung. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13), which plays the contract in this waker's header. STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person, in a proof run (horde wake run -Proof -Target <session id> -Once): a nudge asked for a session whose box is not empty, or that is mid-turn, types nothing and answers busy.

state.limit.evidence: mail state gives each row limited (yes, no, unknown) and limitedUntil (a time, or null), as the fleet's command has since its main 93df6a2. Against the fake, a row saying yes read limited with its time, no read not limited, and unknown - or a row of a command too old to say - read unknown. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13). STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person: a session whose last turn ended in a usage-limit error reads limited yes with the reset time the error named, and a working one reads no.

state.between-turns.evidence: mail state gives each row betweenTurns (yes, no, unknown), as the fleet's command has since its main 5224296: yes when the session's status says busy only because background work is running and its own turn has ended. Against the fake, a row saying yes, no and unknown each read as that, and a row of a command too old to say read unknown. UNVERIFIED: shown against the fake only (test/test-waker-conformance.ps1 and test/test-waker-wezfleet.ps1, 2026-10-13). STILL TO BE RUN against the fleet's real command, by a person: a session whose turn has ended while a background agent of its own still runs reads betweenTurns yes with idle yes, and is nudged only once its box has been read empty.
